answer: Gate minting behind a verifiable delay function: each identity must evaluate a strictly sequential computation that consumes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized, producing a proof cheap to verify but slow to generate. Extra cores give no speedup — a lagoon of idle silicon buys nothing — so a single host fronting many personas must run each delay end to end in series. An ivory stack of a thousand fakes costs a thousand sequential delays, not one; elapsed time becomes the scarce gate, and no pigment of borrowed identity lets one machine multiply it.
